issues.legal_issue: Dishonest abuse of public office to obtain an advantage for another, including by causing government property to be parted with, falls within criminal misconduct.
material_facts: The accused was a public servant responsible for land assignments.
He caused government land to be assigned to his brother-in-law without disclosing their relationship and dishonestly understated the trees and their value to meet the rules for assignment.
The courts below found that he understated the extent and value of the trees to help his brother-in-law.
issues.conclusion: Section 5(1)(d) covers a public servant who dishonestly abuses his position to obtain a valuable thing or pecuniary advantage for another; it is not confined to benefits received from a third party and includes wrongful loss caused to the government. The conduct, if established, constitutes an offence under that provision.
issues.legal_principle: A penal statute must be construed strictly: the charged conduct must fall within both the words and the spirit of the enactment, as explained in Dyke v. Elliot, (1872) L.R. 4 P.C. 184. Section 5(1)(d) of the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1947, is to be read in light of the Act’s purpose of preventing bribery and corruption. “Otherwise” covers abuses of official position beyond corrupt or illegal means, but its context and the dishonesty implicit in “abuse” require dishonest intent; innocuous acts are not covered. The provision reaches advantages obtained for another through abuse of office, including conduct causing wrongful loss to government. Ram Krishan v. State of Delhi, [1956] S.C.R. 182, and Dhaneshwar Narain Saxena v. Delhi Administration, [1962] 3 S.C.R. 259, support its broad scope.

predicates.public_servant_misconduct_case: The proceeding concerns alleged criminal misconduct by a public servant.
predicates.public_servant_abused_position_dishonest: The public servant dishonestly used official position for a purpose for which it was not intended.
predicates.advantage_obtained_for_another: The public servant's conduct secured a valuable thing or pecuniary advantage for another person.

issues.definition: When a criminal-misconduct proceeding concerns a public servant who dishonestly abused official position to secure an advantage for another, that conduct is criminal misconduct.

issues.legal_issue: A court deciding an appeal must give each party an opportunity to address material submitted by the opposing party and relied on in making a factual finding.
material_facts: After the appeal was reserved for judgment, the prosecution filed a valuation statement concerning the trees on the assigned land.
The High Court relied on that statement in assessing under-valuation without giving the accused an opportunity to object to it or challenge its reliability.
issues.conclusion: The High Court violated the principles of natural justice by relying on the statement without giving the accused an opportunity to meet it. The valuation finding was set aside and the matter was remitted to the High Court for a revised finding after the parties had an opportunity to address the material.
issues.legal_principle: The principles of natural justice require a court to give all contesting parties an opportunity to address material on which it relies, particularly material bearing on facts. A party must have an opportunity to object to and contest the reliability of material submitted by the opposing party before it is relied on for a finding.

predicates.appeal_from_criminal_conviction: The proceeding is an appeal from a criminal conviction.
predicates.opposing_party_submitted_material: One party submitted material for the court to consider.
predicates.court_relied_on_material_for_factual_fin: The court relied on that material when making a factual finding.
predicates.affected_party_had_no_opportunity_to_cha: The party affected by the material was not given an opportunity to object to or challenge it.

issues.definition: When an appellate court relies on material submitted by one party for a factual finding without giving the affected party an opportunity to challenge it, the finding is set aside and remitted for reconsideration after that opportunity.
